title: Italian language courses
description: Il Laboratorio di lingue moderne - centro linguistico dell'Università della Svizzera italiana - eroga insegnamenti di lingua italiana dal livello A1 al livello B2 del Quadro Comune Europeo di Riferimento per le Lingue (QCER).

blocks.html:
The Laboratory of Modern Languages - USI's University language centre - offers Italian language courses from level A1 to level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).
Each course aims to develop comprehension and production skills, both oral and written.

Italian language courses open to USI community free of charge

Language courses open to USI Alumni and students from other Swiss universities fee-based

Language courses open to external users fee-based

items.title: Why study Italian?
items.html:
• Italian is the official national language of Canton Ticino and the southern valleys of Graubünden;
  • In Switzerland, a high level of proficiency in at least two of the country’s official languages is generally required, together with passive knowledge of the third official language;
  • The Laboratory of Modern Languages offers free language courses to all USI members in order to promote language learning and foster multilingualism within the academic community;
  • A good knowledge of Italian broadens your study and career opportunities;
  • An officially recognised certificate is often a requirement for admission to Università della Svizzera italiana;
  • A high level of proficiency could be a requirement for university Mobility programmes;
  • For students enrolled in the Master’s programme in Cognitive Psychology in Health Communication, Italian language courses allow students to obtain ECTS credits;
  • A good knowledge of Italian is essential for professional integration not only in Canton Ticino but throughout Switzerland. For example, the Federal Act on Medical Professions (LPMed) requires all future doctors to have the necessary language skills to practise their profession.

items.title: Italian language proficiency certifications
items.html:
The main official certifications for the Italian language are CILS, CELI and PLIDA. All examinations follow the CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) levels, from A1 to C2.
